Cross-border contract with Canadian client creates tax and legal complexity
90-day warranty period for full-stack platform with many dependencies
No uptime or performance guarantees but real-time features required
Scope changes billable at $200/hour with no budget cap
Liability cap at $65,000 exposes Developer to full contract value
10-business-day cure period for termination is short

Data protection compliance (GDPR, CCPA) entirely Client's responsibility despite Developer building system

liability_analysis.assessment: Exposes Developer to 100% of contract value for any liability
excluded_damages: Indirect, consequential, incidental, special, or punitive
liability_analysis.note: Reasonable exclusions but cap is still full contract value

cross_border_concerns: Client is Canadian company, Developer location not specified
Disputes litigated in Developer's jurisdiction (contradiction if Developer not in Ontario)
Currency is USD but Client is Canadian (exchange rate risk)
Potential withholding tax issues on payments from Canada
Developer may need to register for Canadian GST/HST
Contract enforcement across borders can be expensive
Canadian privacy laws (PIPEDA) may apply differently than US
payment_risks: $20,000 non-refundable deposit (31%) before any work delivered
If Client terminates early, deposit is lost
Payment milestones reasonably tied to deliverables
Net 10 day payment terms are aggressive for $20,000 invoices
Late payment penalty of 24% APR is reasonable deterrent
Scope changes at $200/hour with no cap could inflate costs significantly
Completed milestone payments non-refundable even if project cancelled
technical_complexity_risks: Full-stack development with React, TypeScript, Node.js, PostgreSQL, Redis
Real-time features (WebSockets) add complexity and potential failure points
Interactive data visualization with D3.js/Chart.js requires significant frontend expertise
Survey system with complex logic for creation, distribution, and response collection
Email notification system could face deliverability issues
File processing (CSV, Excel) can have many edge cases and errors
Scheduled jobs require reliable infrastructure and monitoring
AWS deployment with multiple services (EC2, RDS, S3) increases complexity
timeline_concerns: 4 months (16 weeks) for full-stack platform is aggressive
Only 2 weeks for requirements and design (likely insufficient)
5 weeks for frontend with React, TypeScript, D3.js, WebSockets (tight)
5 weeks for backend API, database, Redis, email, file processing (very tight)
Only 2 weeks for integration and testing (insufficient for complex platform)
No buffer for unexpected issues or scope changes
Developer not liable for delays from Client feedback or technical issues
Timeline adjustment requires mutual agreement (good protection)
warranty_concerns: 90-day warranty for full-stack platform with many third-party dependencies
Must fix defects in Developer's code for 90 days post-launch
No warranty for specific performance metrics despite real-time features
No warranty for future technology compatibility
Warranty excludes Client-caused issues and third-party problems
data_protection_risks: Client responsible for GDPR and CCPA compliance
Developer builds the system but doesn't warrant compliance
Survey platform likely collects personal data requiring compliance
Developer must notify Client of breaches within 48 hours
GDPR requires 72-hour notification to authorities (tighter than contract)
Client handles regulatory notifications but may blame Developer
Security measures defined as 'reasonable' which is vague
support_limitations: Only bug fixes for Developer's code included
48-hour response for critical issues (not resolution time)
ip_concerns: Full IP transfer to Client upon final payment (good for Client)
Developer retains pre-existing code and tools (reasonable)
Client gets perpetual license to Developer's pre-existing materials
Open-source usage allowed except GPL/AGPL without approval
Client responsible for ongoing license compliance

developer_indemnifies_for: Developer's breach, negligence, or law violations
indemnification_analysis.assessment: Reasonably balanced with Client taking data/regulatory risk

termination_risks: Either party can terminate with 15 days notice before work begins
After work begins, need material breach + 10 day cure
10-day cure period is short for complex technical issues
$20,000 deposit at risk if termination occurs early in project
Client pays pro-rata for work in progress (reasonable)
acceptance_testing: Automatic acceptance if no rejection within 10 days
Must reject in writing with detailed defect list
Developer must remedy material defects at no charge
Definition of 'material defects' vs minor issues could be disputed
dispute_resolution_confusion: If Developer not in Ontario, creates conflict
Should specify exact jurisdiction for litigation
Cross-border litigation can be very expensive
rationale: This contract has reasonable protections (liability cap, mutual indemnification, appropriate warranty exclusions) but significant concerns remain. The $20,000 non-refundable deposit (31%) is high, the cross-border nature adds tax and legal complexity, and the 4-month timeline is aggressive for the scope. The 90-day warranty period is long, and the scope change provisions allow unlimited additions at $200/hour. The dispute resolution clause is confusing (Ontario law but Developer's jurisdiction). With modifications, this could be acceptable.
required_changes_to_accept: Clarify dispute resolution jurisdiction - should match governing law (Ontario)
Add cap on scope change work ($20,000 additional maximum)
Extend timeline to 5 months (20 weeks) with 2-week buffer
Extend cure period from 10 to 15 days
Clarify tax responsibilities (who pays withholding, GST/HST)
Extend acceptance testing to 15 business days (3 weeks)
Add provision that AWS infrastructure costs are reimbursable or included in fee
Specify that real-time features are 'best effort' due to complexity
Add milestone for 'substantial completion' before final $10,000 payment
deal_breakers: If Client insists on keeping $20,000 non-refundable deposit
If cross-border tax issues cannot be clarified
If scope change cap cannot be negotiated
If timeline cannot be extended to realistic 5-6 months
strengths_of_contract: Liability capped at contract value with appropriate exclusions
IP transfers cleanly to Client with Developer retaining tools
Client takes data protection compliance responsibility
Developer not liable for delays from Client or technical issues
